title: bootstrap HSM enrollment and pre-upgrade secret reconciliation hooks for safe rollback
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: private deployments frequently require an initial, idempotent enrollment flow for customer HSMs and a safe upgrade path for KMS-backed secrets. This PR implements a bootstrap enrollment controller, Helm pre-upgrade hooks to reconcile sealed secrets to a new envelope key, Terraform idempotency fixes for kms modules, and an explicit rollback-safe secret staging flow. Changes are focused on automation so operator work during upgrades is minimal and recoverable. Scope: (1) A new 'kms-enroller' component that runs once per cluster to generate an envelope key in Vault Transit or directly provision a HSM-wrapped key via PKCS#11 attestation; (2) Helm chart hooks: pre-upgrade job that validates cluster keys and moves sealedsecret payloads to a staging namespace while writing reconciliation records to a ConfigMap; post-upgrade job to switch active key and re-seal payloads; (3) Terraform module tweaks to make kms resources fully idempotent across apply/destroy cycles and expose new outputs for enrollment tokens; (4) A rollback-aware operator hook that keeps previous envelope key active for 72 hours and automatically reverts if checks fail. Security model: enrollment uses short-lived enrollment tokens (rotating via Terraform state), attestation to HSM via PKCS#11 and TPM endorsement where available, and Vault policies scoped to transit:encrypt/decrypt only. Migration path: - dry-run mode available on the enroller to simulate re-seal operations; - operators can opt into the automatic migration or run manual reconcile via the installer CLI; - automatic fallbacks to previous key ensure zero-downtime during partial failures. Testing and verification: integration tests added under test/integration/kms-enroll that mock HSM via SoftHSM and an end-to-end using a temporarily provisioned Vault instance. Canary rollout notes: default behavior is off behind a feature flag RELEASE_KMS_BOOTSTRAP; when enabled the installer performs a dry-run and creates a /bootstrap-ready ConfigMap before any mutation. Checklist: - [x] implement kms-enroller controller and CLI hooks - [x] pre/post-upgrade Helm hooks and job templates - [x] Terraform idempotency fixes and module outputs - [x] integration tests and CI pipeline updates - [x] documentation and upgrade notes. Risks: HSM attestation failure modes are explicitly caught and reported; fallback preserves previous envelope key to avoid irrecoverable secret loss. See linked linear items for rollout schedule and stakeholder sign-offs.

release_notes: Added an idempotent KMS enrollment flow for private deployments with Helm pre/post-upgrade hooks, Terraform idempotency fixes, and a rollback-safe staging path for secrets. Feature gated behind RELEASE_KMS_BOOTSTRAP. Operators should read docs/private-deployments/kms-enrollment.md before enabling.
notes: Hotfix consideration: if customers run a 3rd-party HSM that doesn't support PKCS#11, the enroller will fall back to a manual enrollment path documented in the README.
Operational runbook added to docs with 'force-rollback' CLI and detection thresholds for automated revert.
Backwards compatibility: sealed secrets encrypted with previous envelope keys remain readable until TTL expires; controller keeps previous key active for 72 hours by default.
